subject: ENGLISH
title: இன்றைய குறிப்புகள்: Unit 1: Hospitality || அலகு 1: விருந்தோம்பல் & Prose: The Gift || உரைநடை: பரிசு

quiz.q: Who was hungry and looking for something to eat at the beginning of the story?
quiz.ex: The story begins with an old beggar who was very hungry and went to a big house looking for food.

quiz.q: How did the first house look from the outside?
quiz.ex: The first house the beggar approached was described as very big and luxurious with a beautiful garden.

quiz.q: What could the beggar smell as he neared the big house?
quiz.ex: As the old man neared the luxurious house, he could smell the aroma of tasty food.

quiz.q: Who opened the door when the beggar knocked on the big house?
quiz.ex: A well-dressed man opened the door and his face shrank on seeing the old beggar.

quiz.q: How many days had passed since the old beggar last had food?
quiz.ex: The old man replied in a feeble voice that it had been two days since he had any food.

quiz.q: What did the rich man shout at the old beggar?
options: "Do you think I am running a free food service?"
quiz.ex: The rich man got angry and arrogantly shouted that he was not running a free food service.

quiz.q: What happened to the door of the rich man's house?
quiz.ex: The rich man told the beggar to get out of his sight and slammed the door forcefully.

quiz.q: What did the beggar see a lady doing in the compound of the first house?
options: Dropping banana leaves with food in the trash can
quiz.ex: While walking away, the old man saw a lady throwing banana leaves with leftover food into the trash can, which made him sad.

quiz.q: When the beggar knocked on the second house, what did the voice from inside say?
options: "Nobody is home. Try the next house."
quiz.ex: After repeated knocks, a voice from the second house lied by saying 'Nobody is home'.

quiz.q: Why did the man in the second house deny food to the beggar?
options: He did not have enough food for himself
Because the richest man of the village denied it
quiz.ex: The man asked how he could be expected to help when the richest man of the village himself had denied help.

quiz.q: Where did the tired old man sit and soon fall asleep?
options: On a bench in the park
quiz.ex: Being exhausted and unable to walk anymore, the old man sat under a tree and soon fell asleep.

quiz.q: Who woke the old man up from his sleep under the tree?
quiz.ex: A poor man wearing shabby clothes woke him up and enquired why he was lying there.

quiz.q: What did the old man say to Kaliyan when he was invited to his hut?
options: "I don't want to be a burden to you."
quiz.ex: The old man was considerate and told the poor man that he didn't want to be a burden and just needed some food.

quiz.q: How did Kaliyan's hut look?
options: Very small and barely enough for the family
quiz.ex: The hut was very small, without any furniture, and barely enough for the poor family.

quiz.q: Where did Kaliyan work?
quiz.ex: When Kaliyan introduced himself, he mentioned that he worked in the nearby farm.

quiz.q: Who is Kaliyan's wife?
quiz.ex: Kaliyan introduced his family, mentioning his wife's name as Viji.

quiz.q: What are the names of Kaliyan's children?
quiz.ex: Kaliyan's children were named Gopi and Rathika.

quiz.q: What did Kaliyan do as soon as the old man entered the hut?
options: He helped the man wash his face and hands
quiz.ex: Showing true hospitality, Kaliyan helped the tired old man wash his face and hands before the meal.

quiz.q: What dish did Viji serve the old man?
quiz.ex: Viji served gruel (a thin, watery porridge) to the old man and her family.

quiz.q: From what kind of vessel was the gruel served?
quiz.ex: Viji served the gruel from a simple earthen pot, showing their poor economic condition.

quiz.q: Who was served first during the dinner?
quiz.ex: Respecting the guest, Viji served the hungry old man first before her own family.

quiz.q: Where did the old man sleep that night?
options: On a mat laid by Kaliyan
quiz.ex: After dinner, Kaliyan laid a simple mat for the old man to sleep on.

quiz.q: What surprising instruction did the old man give Kaliyan's family the next morning?
quiz.ex: The next morning, the beggar surprisingly asked Kaliyan's family to pack all their things.

quiz.q: What was the real identity of the old beggar?
options: A landlord from a nearby town
quiz.ex: The old man revealed that he was not a beggar but a wealthy landlord from a nearby town.

quiz.q: What happened to the landlord's wife and son?
options: They were living in the city
quiz.ex: The landlord mentioned that his wife and son had died two years ago, leaving him alone.

quiz.q: Why did the landlord disguise himself as a beggar?
options: He wanted to find someone to take care of his wealth and continue his service
He was running away from enemies
quiz.ex: He disguised himself to find a genuinely kind-hearted person who could inherit his wealth and continue helping the poor.

quiz.q: How did Kaliyan initially react to the landlord's offer?
options: He was extremely greedy and grabbed it
quiz.ex: Kaliyan was initially reluctant (hesitant) to accept such a huge gift from the landlord.

quiz.q: What does the word 'Twig' mean according to the Pictionary?
options: A small, thin branch of a tree or bush
quiz.ex: A twig is defined as a small, thin branch of a tree or bush.

quiz.q: Choose the correct meaning for 'Shadow'.
options: A reflective surface like a mirror
The dark area seen under an object in light
quiz.ex: A shadow is the dark area that is cast by an object blocking the light.

quiz.q: What is 'Gruel'?
quiz.ex: Gruel is a very simple, thin, and watery porridge, usually eaten by the poor.

quiz.q: Find the meaning for the word 'Disguise'.
options: To change the appearance to hide identity
To wear new clothes for a festival
quiz.ex: Disguise means changing one's appearance so that others cannot recognize their true identity.

quiz.q: Who is a 'Guest'?
options: A person who attacks the house
A person who is invited to a function or to stay at one's house
A person who begs on the street
quiz.ex: A guest is someone invited to visit or stay in a person's home.

quiz.q: According to the glossary, what does 'shrank' mean in the context 'The man's face shrank'?
quiz.ex: In this context, 'shrank' denotes an adverse, disgusted, or unwelcoming reaction on the rich man's face.

quiz.q: What is the synonym for the word 'feeble'?
quiz.ex: Feeble means weak. The old man had a feeble voice because he hadn't eaten for two days.

quiz.q: What does the word 'denied' mean?
quiz.ex: Denied means to refuse to give or grant something.

quiz.q: The poor man was wearing 'shabby' clothes. What does 'shabby' mean?
quiz.ex: Shabby refers to items, especially clothes, that are old, worn out, and in poor condition.

quiz.q: Kaliyan was 'reluctant' to accept the landlord's offer. 'Reluctant' means:
quiz.ex: Reluctant means feeling hesitant or unwilling to do something.

quiz.q: The old man 'persuaded' Kaliyan and his family. What is the meaning of 'persuaded'?
quiz.ex: Persuaded means convincing someone to do or believe something through reasoning.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: The rich man ______ at the beggar.
quiz.ex: According to the book back exercise, the rich man shouted at the beggar to get out.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: A man in ______ clothes stopped near him.
quiz.ex: Kaliyan, who approached the old man, was wearing shabby clothes.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: The hut was very ______.
quiz.ex: Kaliyan's hut was described as very small and barely enough for his family.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: Kaliyan worked in a ______.
quiz.ex: Kaliyan mentioned that he worked in the farm nearby.

quiz.q: Match the following: 'trash can' is correctly matched with...
quiz.ex: In the story, the lady dropped banana leaves with wasted food into the trash can.

quiz.q: Match the following: 'gruel' is correctly matched with...
quiz.ex: Viji served the gruel from an earthen pot.

quiz.q: Grammar: When we add the suffix '-less', it gives the meaning...
options: a person who does an action
quiz.ex: The suffix '-less' changes the root word to mean 'without' (e.g., toothless = without teeth).

quiz.q: Grammar: When we add the suffix '-ful', it gives the meaning...
quiz.ex: The suffix '-ful' changes the root word to mean 'full of' (e.g., joyful = full of joy).

quiz.q: Grammar: When we add the suffix '-er', it denotes...
options: a person who does the action
quiz.ex: The suffix '-er' signifies a person performing an action (e.g., singer = a person who sings).

quiz.q: Grammar: When we add the suffix '-ment', it denotes...
options: a person who does the action
quiz.ex: The suffix '-ment' converts a verb into a noun, denoting the name of the action (e.g., judgement).

quiz.q: Join the word with correct suffix: dance + ______
quiz.ex: dance + er = dancer (a person who dances).

quiz.q: Join the word with correct suffix: entertain + ______
quiz.ex: entertain + ment = entertainment (the act of entertaining).

quiz.q: Join the word with correct suffix: fear + ______
quiz.ex: fear + ful = fearful (full of fear).

quiz.q: Form a new word with the appropriate suffix: peace + ______
quiz.ex: peace + ful = peaceful.

quiz.q: Form a new word with the appropriate suffix: govern + ______
quiz.ex: govern + ment = government.

quiz.q: Add appropriate suffix for 'A person one who teaches'. (Root word: teach)
quiz.ex: teach + er = teacher.

quiz.q: Add appropriate suffix for 'Having no money'. (Root word: penny)
quiz.ex: penny + less = penniless (meaning without a penny/money).

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): The old man left the second house feeling happy.
Reason (R): The man in the second house refused to give him food.
options: A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true
Both A and R are false
quiz.ex: The beggar was sad and disappointed, not happy, because the second house also refused to give him food.

quiz.q: True or False: The rich man gave his leftover food to the old beggar.
options: He gave it the next day
quiz.ex: The rich man denied food entirely and slammed the door, and the lady threw the leftovers in the trash.

quiz.q: What is the primary moral of the story 'The Gift'?
options: You should never talk to strangers
True hospitality comes from a kind heart, not from wealth
quiz.ex: The story shows that despite being poor, Kaliyan's family showed immense love and hospitality, unlike the rich man.

quiz.q: Why didn't the old man tell Kaliyan he was rich on the first night itself?
options: He was afraid of being robbed
He wanted to test their true hospitality and kindness without any expectations
quiz.ex: The landlord disguised himself to test the pure character and genuine hospitality of the people before making them his heirs.

quiz.q: Which of the following actions proved Kaliyan's kindness?
options: He asked the old man for money
He woke up the tired stranger and invited him to share their limited food
He told the stranger to go to the big house
quiz.ex: Despite his own poverty, Kaliyan's gesture to invite a stranger home and offer him their little food showed true kindness.

quiz.q: According to the poem 'Mother Nature', who gives everything to all creatures?
quiz.ex: The poem states 'Look at the hospitality of Mother Nature! It gives everything to all creature.'

quiz.q: In the poem 'Mother Nature', what can you enjoy for free under the tree?
quiz.ex: The lines say 'Enjoy the shadows and fruits for free.'

quiz.q: According to the poem, for whom is there a home under the tree?
quiz.ex: The poem states 'There is a home for bird'.

quiz.q: According to the poem, what knocks with its best for those who care for their guest?
quiz.ex: The lines state 'Fortune knocks with its best, Those who cares for their guest.'

quiz.q: What is the meaning of 'hospitality' as given in the glossary?
options: Taking good care of the guests and visitors
quiz.ex: Hospitality means welcoming and taking good care of guests and visitors.

quiz.q: What does 'refreshing' mean in the poem?
quiz.ex: Refreshing means renewing, as in a place that gives fresh energy.

quiz.q: Identify the rhyming word for 'tree' from the poem.
quiz.ex: In the poem, 'tree' rhymes with 'free' (strangers under the tree, shadows and fruits for free).

quiz.q: Identify the rhyming word for 'bird' from the poem.
quiz.ex: In the poem, 'bird' rhymes with 'herd'.

quiz.q: Identify the rhyming word for 'face' from the poem.
quiz.ex: In the poem, 'face' rhymes with 'race'.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank from the poem: Mother nature gives everything for all ______.
quiz.ex: The poem line is 'It gives everything to all creature.'

quiz.q: Grammar: Which tense is used to show that an event has happened in the past and has present consequences?
quiz.ex: Present Perfect tense connects the past with the present to show actions that have present consequences.

quiz.q: Grammar: What form of the verb is used in the Present Perfect Tense?
quiz.ex: We use the past participle form (e.g., gone, played, written) along with have/has.

quiz.q: Grammar: Which helping verb is used with the pronouns 'he, she, it' in Present Perfect Tense?
quiz.ex: 'Has' is used for third-person singular subjects (he, she, it).

quiz.q: Grammar: Which helping verb is used with the pronouns 'I, you, we, they' in Present Perfect Tense?
quiz.ex: 'Have' is used for I, you, we, and they.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb form: I _________ the Tajmahal.
quiz.ex: With 'I', we use 'have' + past participle 'visited'.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb form: He _________ a house in America.
quiz.ex: With 'He', we use 'has' + past participle 'bought'.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb form: She _________ her exam.
quiz.ex: With 'She', we use 'has' + past participle 'written'.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb form: They _________ in yellow colour.
quiz.ex: With 'They', we use 'have' + past participle 'dressed'.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: I _________ never seen a cobra.
quiz.ex: We use 'have' with the pronoun 'I'.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: He _________ just lost his wallet.
quiz.ex: We use 'has' with the third-person singular pronoun 'He'.

quiz.q: Rewrite the sentence correctly starting with 'She': I have read this story. -> She ______________.
quiz.ex: When changing the subject from 'I' to 'She', the helping verb changes from 'have' to 'has'.

quiz.q: Rewrite the sentence starting with 'We': Shanmathi has given the book. -> We ______________.
quiz.ex: When changing the subject to 'We', the helping verb changes to 'have'.

quiz.q: Change the sentence to present perfect tense: 'She writes a letter to her friend.'
options: She wrote a letter to her friend.
She is writing a letter to her friend.
She has written a letter to her friend.
She have written a letter to her friend.
quiz.ex: 'writes' (simple present) changes to 'has written' (present perfect) for the subject 'She'.

quiz.q: Change the sentence to present perfect tense: 'Mohamad loses his purse in the crowd.'
options: Mohamad lost his purse in the crowd.
Mohamad has lost his purse in the crowd.
Mohamad have lost his purse in the crowd.
Mohamad is losing his purse in the crowd.
quiz.ex: The past participle of 'lose' is 'lost'. Since Mohamad is singular, we use 'has'.

quiz.q: Change the sentence to present perfect tense: 'They eat all the bananas themselves.'
options: They ate all the bananas themselves.
They have eaten all the bananas themselves.
They has eaten all the bananas themselves.
They are eating all the bananas themselves.
quiz.ex: With 'They', we use 'have'. The past participle of 'eat' is 'eaten'.

quiz.q: Choose the appropriate verb to complete: John has __________ a letter to his father. (drank / written / won / taken)
quiz.ex: You write a letter. So, 'written' is the correct past participle here.

quiz.q: Choose the appropriate verb to complete: We have __________ the first prize twice in 2 years. (written / taken / won / gone)
quiz.ex: Prizes are won. The correct past participle is 'won'.

quiz.q: Choose the appropriate verb to complete: Vithya and Fathima have _________ briyani for the party. (gone / prepared / taken / written)
quiz.ex: Food is prepared. Hence 'prepared' is the correct word.

options: a person who does an action
quiz.ex: The suffix '-less' changes the root word to mean 'without' (e.g., toothless = without teeth).

quiz.q: Let Us Listen: When do we celebrate the Independence day?
quiz.ex: India celebrates its Independence Day on the 15th of August.

quiz.q: Let Us Speak: Which phrase is best used to ask someone's identity on a phone call?
options: May I know who is speaking?
Tell me your name right now.
quiz.ex: 'May I know who is speaking?' is a polite and structured way to ask someone's identity over the phone.

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): True hospitality means spending a lot of money on your guests.
Reason (R): Kaliyan spent a lot of money to buy luxurious food for the old beggar.
options: A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
Both A and R are true
Both A and R are false
quiz.ex: Both are false. Hospitality is about a kind heart, not wealth. Kaliyan did not have money; he shared his simple gruel.

quiz.q: HOTS: Why does the poet refer to Nature as 'Mother Nature' in the poem?
options: Because nature nurtures, protects, and gives unconditionally like a mother
quiz.ex: Like a mother who selflessly feeds and protects her children, Nature provides shade, food, and shelter to all creatures unconditionally.

quiz.q: HOTS: What happens to a person who welcomes guests with a 'smiling face' according to the poem?
options: They win hearts in life's race
quiz.ex: A smiling welcome creates a positive bond, helping a person win the love and hearts of others in the journey of life.
